task: FV2-028 — Flutter Android text-history chrome visibility while scrolling
summary: Added a widget regression requiring the workspace header and text composer to retain their bounds during a vertical history scroll and ensuring the navigation drawer stays closed. Focused test, analyzer, full Flutter suite, and a controlled Android API 35 visual acceptance all pass.

checks.name: Focused text history scroll and fixed chrome regression
checks.command: flutter test --no-pub test/workspace_screen_test.dart --plain-name 'opens text history at latest and advances its read cursor'
checks.observation: The test confirms the message list scroll offset changes while the workspace header and text composer bounds remain unchanged; a vertical drag does not open the navigation drawer.

checks.name: Full Flutter test suite
checks.observation: All 585 tests passed against the final test source.

checks.name: Android text history scroll visual acceptance
checks.observation: From a stable Text-channel screen with the drawer closed, a controlled vertical swipe visibly moved the history to older messages while the workspace header and composer remained on screen. UIAutomator reported the channel subtitle at [179,217][450,262] and composer at [21,2174][1059,2316]; the navigation drawer's close control was absent. The earlier inconsistent captures were resolved by repeating from this controlled starting state. No message was sent or edited. Read-cursor state was not inspected.

limitations: Samsung/Gboard login behavior, history pagination, backend read-cursor state, and remaining composer/attachment states remain open under FV2-002.
